title: Column deviation bound from cumulative regret
statement: Let $G$ be a two-player game with $M$ row actions and $N$ column actions, and let $T>0$. In each of $T$ rounds, let $p_t$ and $q_t$ be mixed strategies for the row and column players, respectively. For any $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{R}$ and column action $j'$, if the cumulative utility from always choosing $j'$ against the row strategies, minus the cumulative expected column utility under the round-by-round strategy pairs, is at most $\varepsilon T$, then under the empirical joint distribution of those pairs, the column player's expected utility from choosing $j'$ against the row marginal is at most the expected column utility plus $\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: $G$ is a game with $M$ row actions and $N$ column actions
Each round's row and column strategies are probability distributions on their respective action sets
The stated cumulative column deviation utility difference is at most $\varepsilon T$
replaced:
Let $G$ be a finite two-player game with column utility $u_c$ over $M$ row actions and
$N$ column actions, and consider $T > 0$ rounds of play in which the row player uses the
mixed strategy $p_t$ and the column player the mixed strategy $q_t$ at round $t$. Fix
$\varepsilon \in \bbr$ and a pure column action $j'$, and suppose the column player's
cumulative external regret against always playing $j'$ is at most $\varepsilon T$:
\[
  \sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i}(p_t)_i\, u_c(i,j')
  \;-\; \sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i,j}(p_t)_i (q_t)_j\, u_c(i,j)
  \;\le\; \varepsilon T.
\]
Then in the empirical joint distribution $\sigma$ of the play, deviating to $j'$ gains
at most $\varepsilon$ over the expected utility:
$\mathrm{colDevUtil}(\sigma, G, j') \le \mathrm{colExpUtil}(\sigma, G) + \varepsilon$.
This is the column half of \texttt{empiricalJoint\_isApproxCCE}, mirroring
\texttt{empiricalJoint\_row\_deviation\_le}.
